mainTopic: When a wife who receives a share of her husband's property loses her כתובה: the refutation of the אמוראים, רב נחמן's partnership rule, the healthy-husband question, and gifts of produce versus land
overview: The משנה teaches that if a man divides his property among his sons and gives his wife a share, she loses her כתובה. The גמרא first calls this one of the 'leniencies of כתובה.' It then shows from רבי יוסי's words, backed by a ברייתא of רבי יהודה, that the תנא קמא requires the wife's presence and active acceptance. That refutes all three אמוראים, who thought her silence was enough. רב נחמן gives his own view: once the husband made her a partner among the sons, she loses her כתובה. רבא asks whether this also applies to a healthy husband, and the question stays תיקו. In a real case, רב חסדא and רב נחמן conclude that a gift of produce alone, which counts as movable property, does not cost her the כתובה. Only a share in land, even one palm tree, does. A final case begins: a dying man gave thirds to two daughters and his wife, and one daughter died first. רב פפי's first thought is that the wife takes only her third, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: This ruling is a leniency of the marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: The explanation offered just before ends by saying that the משנה is teaching one of the special leniencies that apply to a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages taught here one of the leniencies of a marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation offered just before this line. It says the משנה is describing a special leniency for the husband regarding the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary lender would not lose the money he is owed just because he quietly let the borrower divide up his property. A wife can lose her כתובה this way, so the rule is easier on the husband. That is why it is called one of the קולי כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leniencies of the marriage contract: rules that make it easier for the husband or his heirs
The marriage contract and the money it promises the wife
They taught here, meaning the משנה is teaching this

phrases.english: And of the leniencies of the marriage contract they taught here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the explanation of the משנה offered just before this line
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing the כתובה in this case is a special leniency of כתובה that does not apply to an ordinary debt.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's words imply the first opinion needs both writing and acceptance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the same משנה. If he says acceptance alone is enough, then the תנא קמא must require both writing and acceptance. That goes against all the explanations given.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי יוסי says, if she accepted it upon herself, even if he did not write anything for her, she loses her כתובה. This implies that the first תנא holds that both writing and acceptance are needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanations of the אמוראים using a later line in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says acceptance alone is enough, even without writing. That suggests he is arguing with the תנא קמא, so the תנא קמא must need both. The אמוראים had assumed that the wife's silence is enough and no active acceptance is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
She accepted it upon herself, meaning she agreed to the division
By inference, from what is implied
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
The husband's writing and the wife's acceptance

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
If she accepted it upon herself,
phrases.notes: She accepted her husband's division of the property among the sons.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כָּתַב לָהּ –
phrases.english: even though he did not write for her
phrases.notes: He did not write her any land at all.

phrases.english: she has lost her marriage contract.
By inference, the first tanna holds:
writing and acceptance are both required!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanations of the משנה, which assumed her silence is enough
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of רב, שמואל, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's statement that acceptance alone is enough implies that the תנא קמא needs both writing and acceptance, so silence would not be enough.

steps.title: Suggestion: the whole משנה is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out. Maybe the whole משנה follows רבי יוסי, so there is no separate תנא קמא who needs both conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: the whole משנה is רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the challenge. It also sets up the next step, which will reject this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole משנה is רבי יוסי, then the first part of the משנה is also his view. On that reading, writing alone or acceptance alone is each enough. Then no one in the משנה requires both, and the inference falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggested answer
All of it, the entire משנה

phrases.english: And if you would say:
the whole of it is Rabbi Yosei;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a defense against the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the whole משנה to one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first part of the משנה is a separate opinion that requires both writing and acceptance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יוסי, so either writing or acceptance alone would be enough.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's ברייתא shows the first opinion needs presence and acceptance
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: she loses her כתובה only if she was present and accepted. If either is missing, she keeps it. So the first opinion really is separate and stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said, when does this apply? When she was there and accepted it. But if she was there and did not accept, or accepted and was not there, she has not lost her כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that the whole משנה is רבי יוסי by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה explains the first opinion as needing both her presence and her active acceptance. This shows that the תנא קמא is a separate opinion from רבי יוסי, and he is stricter. So the challenge from step 2 comes back in full force.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא: introduces a source that contradicts
When? It limits when the rule applies
She was there, present at the division

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When? When she was there and accepted it upon herself;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָיְתָה שָׁם וְלֹא קִבְּלָה עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: but if she was there and did not accept it upon herself,
or accepted it upon herself but was not there
she has not lost her marriage contract!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the whole משנה is רבי יוסי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's ברייתא shows a separate first opinion that needs both presence and acceptance, so silence is not enough.

steps.title: All the explanations are refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the challenge stands against all the explanations of the אמוראים. It is a full תיובתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refutation of all of them! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the explanations of all the אמוראים have been refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escape route was blocked, so nothing is left to defend the view that her silence is enough. The גמרא first states the refutation and then confirms it with the single word תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a challenge with no answer
Of all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's first opinion needs the wife to be present and to actively accept the division. Her silence alone does not make her lose her כתובה, so all three explanations were refuted.

phrases.english: A refutation of all of them!
phrases.notes: That's all three: רב, שמואל, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the objection cycle that began in step 2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explanations of all three אמוראים are refuted.

steps.title: רבא asks רב נחמן for his own view
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists the three opinions and asks רב נחמן what he himself holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Here is רב's view, here is שמואל's view, here is רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view. What does the Master hold?
steps.whatsHappening: After the refutation, רבא asks רב נחמן for his own opinion. This sets up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has heard three explanations of this משנה, and all of them were refuted. He wants to know how רב נחמן understands the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Master: a respectful way to say 'you'
What does he hold? What is his opinion?

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
Here is Rav, here is Shmuel,
here is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina.
The Master, what does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a new position after the earlier explanations were refuted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב נחמן's own understanding of when the wife loses her כתובה

steps.title: רב נחמן: making her a partner with the sons costs her the marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that once the husband made his wife a partner among the sons, she has lost her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For I say, since he made her a partner among the sons, she has lost her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own reason for why the wife loses her כתובה in the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן explains the loss by looking at what the husband did. He gave her a share alongside the sons, which makes her a partner in the inheritance. That is why she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: For I say: introduces the speaker's own reasoning
Partner
He made her

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's view: once the husband made her a partner with the sons, she loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: He said to him: For I say:
since he made her a partner among the sons
she has lost her marriage contract.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Once the husband made her a partner among the sons, she has lost her כתובה.

steps.title: A second report confirms רב נחמן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי reports in רב נחמן's name that once the husband made his wife a partner among the sons, she loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: once he made her a partner among the sons, she lost her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that what רב נחמן just told רבא was also passed down as a formal ruling in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. The point is that this was not a passing comment: רב נחמן's answer was taught as a fixed ruling by a student. This strengthens the ruling from Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: a second report of the same teaching
Partner, someone who gets a share
She lost her כתובה, her right to collect her marriage-contract money

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
Once he made her a partner among the sons,
she has lost her marriage contract.
phrases.notes: She can no longer collect her כתובה money from the estate. The share she got takes its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב נחמן's answer from Step 7 with a second, formal report.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a wife made a partner among the sons loses her כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A separate report by רב יוסף בר מניומי in רב נחמן's name.

steps.title: רבא asks: what if the husband is healthy?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the wife also loses her כתובה when a healthy husband divides his property this way, or only when he is on his deathbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: what about a healthy man? Do we say that only with a dying man does she know he has nothing else, so she is giving up her claim? But with a healthy man, she may think he will acquire more property later. Or perhaps, since right now he has nothing else, it is the same?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question and lays out both sides: does רב נחמן's rule also apply when the husband is healthy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a dying man, she knows this is all there is, so accepting a share means giving up her כתובה. With a healthy man, she might accept the share only because she expects him to earn more, which she could collect from later. The other side says that what counts is the moment: right now he has nothing else, so accepting still means giving up.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question that needs a decision
A healthy person
A person on his deathbed
She gave up (waived) her claim
Or perhaps: brings the other side of the question

phrases.english: Rava asked:
With a healthy man, what is the law?
Do we say:
it is only with a man on his deathbed
that she knows he has nothing else, and so she is giving up her claim,
but with a healthy man
she thinks he will go on to acquire more property;
phrases.notes: So she is not really giving up her כתובה. She plans to collect it from what he gets later.

phrases.english: or perhaps,
right now, at any rate, he has nothing else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב נחמן's confirmed ruling and asks whether it also covers a healthy husband.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a wife lose her כתובה when a healthy husband (not a dying one) makes her a partner among the sons?

steps.title: The question is left open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבא's question unanswered: תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide רבא's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of רבא's question make sense, and no source settles it. So the case of a healthy husband stays an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: For a dying husband, רב נחמן rules that she loses her כתובה. For a healthy husband, the question is left open (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a wife loses her כתובה when a healthy husband makes her a partner remains undecided.

steps.title: A real case: a third of the produce to the wife
steps.stepSummary: A dying man gave half his estate to each daughter and a third of the produce to his wife. רב חסדא asks רב נחמן what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said: 'Half to my daughter, half to my other daughter, and a third to my wife, in produce.' רב נחמן came to סורא and went in to רב חסדא, who asked him: in a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story and sets up a question: does a wife who got only a share of the produce lose her כתובה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of case. Earlier the wife got a share of the property itself. Here she gets only produce. This sets up whether רב נחמן's rule still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
A third
Produce, fruit that the land yields
Happened to come, arrived
In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
"Half to my daughter,
and half to my other daughter,
and a third to my wife, in produce."
Rav Nachman happened to come to Sura.
He went in to Rav Chisda.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא מַאי?
phrases.english: He said to him: In a case like this, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Here רב חסדא is the one asking, and רב נחמן answers in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case that tests רב נחמן's rule when the wife gets only produce.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a wife who receives only a third of the produce lose her כתובה?

steps.title: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: even one palm tree is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers with שמואל's rule: even if he gave her only one palm tree for its fruit, she loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what שמואל said: even if he gave her nothing but one palm tree for its fruit, she has lost her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by quoting שמואל, who says that even a tiny share makes the wife lose her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule shows that the size of the gift does not matter. Even one tree for its fruit is enough. רב נחמן seems to use this to say the wife in our case also loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave ownership, transferred rights
A palm tree
For its fruit

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
Even if he gave her ownership of
nothing but one palm tree for its fruit,
she has lost her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question by quoting שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Following שמואל, even a very small gift, like one palm tree for its fruit, makes her lose her כתובה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a tree is land, but produce is not
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא points out that שמואל's case involved a tree attached to the land, while here the wife got only produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: maybe שמואל said that there, because he gave her rights in the land itself. Here, it is only produce!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges the comparison to שמואל: the cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A palm tree is attached to the ground, so giving it means giving a piece of the land. In our case she gets only produce, with no part of the land itself. So שמואל's rule may not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, maybe: introduces a way to limit a source
The land itself
Produce only

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָתָם –
phrases.english: He said to him: Say that Shmuel said it there
because he gave her rights in the land itself;
phrases.notes: The palm tree is planted in the ground, so it counts as part of the land.

phrases.english: here, it is only produce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's use of שמואל's rule for this case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying שמואל's palm tree rule to a wife who got only produce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's case gave her part of the land itself (an attached tree). Produce alone is a different kind of gift, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees: movables do not make her lose her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that produce is movable property, and says he never meant that movables make her lose her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: are you talking about movable property? About movable property I certainly did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן accepts רב חסדא's point. A gift of produce, which is movable, does not make the wife lose her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the כתובה applies only when she is given a share in land, even a tiny one like a single tree. Produce counts as movable property, so in this case she keeps her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property, things that are not land
Certainly

steps.whatToRemember: A wife loses her כתובה when she is given a share in land, even just one palm tree. If she gets only produce (movable property), she keeps her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "a palm tree for its fruit" with "produce." The tree is attached land, so it counts. Loose produce is movable, so it does not.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you talking about movable property?
About movable property I certainly did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן concedes רב חסדא's challenge and limits שמואל's rule to land.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wife given only produce (movable property) keeps her כתובה. Only a share in land makes her lose it.

steps.title: A new case: property split into thirds
steps.stepSummary: A dying man gives one-third of his property to each of his two daughters and one-third to his wife. Then one of the daughters dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said: give one-third to my daughter, one-third to my other daughter, and one-third to my wife. One of his daughters died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out the facts of a new case. This is setup: it prepares the question of what the wife now collects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the last case (steps 11-14), where the wife got only produce, here she gets a real share of the property itself, just like the daughters. The daughter died before her father, so her third goes back to him. This raises the question of what the wife now collects: only her third, or also her כתובה from the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: One-third
Daughter (here, 'my daughter')
Wife
Died

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
phrases.notes: He is on his deathbed, talking to the people around him.

phrases.english: "One-third to my daughter,
and one-third to my other daughter,
and one-third to my wife."
One of his daughters died.
phrases.notes: She died before her father, so her third goes back to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case right after the produce case. This time the wife gets actual land, so שמואל's rule from step 12 seems to apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facts only: thirds to two daughters and the wife, and one daughter died first.

steps.title: רב פפי's first thought: she gets only her third
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי at first thinks the wife takes only her one-third and cannot collect her כתובה from the rest of the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי thought to say: she takes only one-third.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives his first opinion: the wife receives her one-third and nothing more. The wording 'thought to say' tells us this view will be challenged next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning follows the rule of רב נחמן from step 7: once the wife was made a partner alongside the daughters, she gave up her כתובה. So she cannot collect her כתובה from the two-thirds left to the daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say: a first thought that is usually overturned
She takes or collects
The money a husband owes his wife, paid from his estate when he dies

steps.confusionAlert: Don't treat this as the final ruling. 'סבר למימר' almost always means the גמרא is about to reject the idea.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi thought to say:
She takes only one-third.
phrases.notes: He means she gets her third but cannot also collect her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first ruling on the case from step 15, using רב נחמן's partnership rule from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First thought: the wife gets only her one-third, because sharing the land with the daughters made her lose her כתובה.
